criterion: Does a general engine developer need this capability, and can Colosseum provide it correctly within the 1.0 architecture?

decisions.reason: Engine developers need to compare and validate ordinary UCI pondering behavior under real game clocks; the shared runner already owns the complete protocol.
decisions.scope: Explicit --ponder on match, sprt, calibrate, spsa and tournament run; clock controls only; default off; recorded in resolved configuration, run record and result.

decisions.reason: Chess960 developers need it, but a trustworthy implementation needs variant-aware position validation, opening ingestion, castling serialization, UCI_Chess960 negotiation, PGN tags and cross-runner fixtures; a flag over standard-chess state would be unsafe.
Harness probing can improve termination and adjudication, but correct WDL/DTZ, 50-move-rule, castling/en-passant, file-set and probe-failure semantics require a dedicated tablebase port and fixtures.
decisions.scope: 1.0 continues forwarding ordinary engine tablebase UCI options without inspecting tablebase files.

decisions.reason: Static round-robin and multi-seed gauntlet cover engine comparison and regression work; Swiss and knockout formats add result-dependent scheduling without a demonstrated engine-development requirement.
decisions.scope: Keep the shared scheduler focused on round-robin and gauntlet.

decisions.reason: Versioned JSON plus PGN and RFC-4180 CSV provide machine interchange, games and tabular results; no missing general consumer contract has been identified.
decisions.scope: New formats require a named consumer and a stable schema requirement.

decisions.reason: Finite fixed-node/depth self-play, deterministic seeds, paired opening randomization, durable resume and PGN already come from match; trainer records and labels are project-specific.
decisions.scope: Document the match recipe; revisit only for concrete generic sharding, deterministic game-ID, deduplication, controlled-randomization or unbounded-horizon requirements.
